p: Name a NoSQL database.
source: Stack Overflow Developer Survey 2024 (Databases)
metric: % of all respondents who did extensive development work in it over the past year
note: Firebase / Firestore mapped to the "Cloud Firestore" line (5.4); SO lists "Firebase Realtime Database" separately at 5.8. 2024 used over 2025 because 2025 dropped CouchDB/Couchbase/RavenDB.

p: Name a relational database management system (RDBMS).
source: Stack Overflow Developer Survey 2024 (Databases)
metric: % of all respondents who did extensive development work in it over the past year
note: 2024 used because 2025 dropped Firebird and TiDB.

p: Name a language that is functional-first (not just multi-paradigm with lambdas).
source: Stack Overflow Developer Survey 2024 (Programming, scripting, and markup languages)
metric: % of all respondents who did extensive development work in it over the past year
note: 2024 used because the 2025 survey dropped Haskell and Clojure. SO "Lisp" covers all Lisps, not only Common Lisp.

p: Name a programming language that runs on the Java Virtual Machine (JVM).
source: Stack Overflow Developer Survey 2024 (Programming, scripting, and markup languages)
metric: % of all respondents who did extensive development work in it over the past year
note: 2024 used because 2025 dropped Clojure. These are overall language usage figures, not JVM-specific ones (Kotlin, for example, includes Android/Native).

p: Name a dynamically typed programming language.
source: Stack Overflow Developer Survey 2024 (Programming, scripting, and markup languages)
metric: % of all respondents who did extensive development work in it over the past year
note: 2024 used because 2025 dropped Clojure and Julia.

p: Name a compiler or compiler toolchain.
source: Stack Overflow Developer Survey 2024 (Embedded technologies)
metric: % of all respondents who did extensive development work with it over the past year (asked in the 'embedded systems and technologies' question)
note: Ambiguous framing: these come from SO's embedded-technologies question, not a general compiler-usage question.

p: Name a public cloud computing provider.
source: Stack Overflow Developer Survey 2024 (Cloud platforms)
metric: % of all respondents who did extensive development work in it over the past year
note: 2024 used: it had a dedicated cloud-platform question; 2025 merged clouds into a tools list and dropped Oracle, Alibaba, Linode, Hetzner, Vultr, OVH.

p: Name a container orchestration platform.
source: Stack Overflow Developer Survey 2025 (Cloud development)
metric: % of all respondents who did extensive development work in it over the past year
note: Only Kubernetes is measured.

p: Name a container engine or runtime.
source: Stack Overflow Developer Survey 2025 (Cloud development)
metric: % of all respondents who did extensive development work in it over the past year

p: Name a message broker or distributed messaging system.
source: Stack Overflow Developer Survey 2024 (Other frameworks and libraries)
metric: % of all respondents who did extensive development work in it over the past year

p: Name an infrastructure-as-code (IaC) or configuration management tool.
source: Stack Overflow Developer Survey 2024 (Other tools)
metric: % of all respondents who did extensive development work in it over the past year
note: 2024 used because 2025 lists only Terraform and Ansible.

p: Name a distributed big-data processing framework or engine.
source: Stack Overflow Developer Survey 2024 (Other frameworks and libraries)
metric: % of all respondents who did extensive development work in it over the past year
note: SO measures "Hadoop" as a whole, not MapReduce specifically.

p: Name a well-known transformer-based language model (or model family).
source: Stack Overflow Developer Survey 2025 (AI models)
metric: % of respondents to the AI-models question who used it for development work in the past year
note: Families are split across lines in SO: Claude = "Claude Sonnet" only; Gemini = "Gemini Flash" (Gemini Reasoning 25.6 is a separate line); DeepSeek = "DeepSeek Reasoning" (DeepSeek General 14.3 is separate). Each value is one SO line, so it is a lower bound for the family. It also measures current dev use, which is a different thing from being well known; BERT, T5 etc. are unmeasured.

p: Name a CI/CD platform or tool.
source: JetBrains State of CI/CD 2025
metric: % of respondents: "Which CI/CD tools are currently used in your organization?"
note: JetBrains/TeamCity 'State of CI/CD 2025' survey (vendor-run; TeamCity is a JetBrains product). Values read from the published chart image state-of-cicd-tool-used-in-organizations-1.png in that post. Azure Pipelines mapped to 'Azure DevOps Server'.

p: Name a CI/CD tool or service.
source: JetBrains State of CI/CD 2025
metric: % of respondents: "Which CI/CD tools are currently used in your organization?"
note: JetBrains/TeamCity 'State of CI/CD 2025' survey (vendor-run; TeamCity is a JetBrains product). Values read from the published chart image state-of-cicd-tool-used-in-organizations-1.png in that post. Azure Pipelines mapped to 'Azure DevOps Server'.

p: Name a text editor or source-code editor (not a full IDE).
source: Stack Overflow Developer Survey 2024 (Integrated development environment)
metric: % of all respondents who did extensive development work in it over the past year
note: 2024 used because 2025 dropped Emacs, Kate, Helix, Geany, BBEdit (2025 adds Cursor 17.9 and Zed 7.3, which this entry therefore lacks).

p: Name a build automation tool.
source: Stack Overflow Developer Survey 2025 (Cloud development: package managers, build tools...)
metric: % of all respondents who did extensive development work in it over the past year
note: CMake, Ant and Bazel are not in the 2025 list.

p: Name a package manager.
source: Stack Overflow Developer Survey 2025 (Cloud development: package managers, build tools...)
metric: % of all respondents who did extensive development work in it over the past year
note: SO labels Maven "Maven (build tool)"; its usage is counted here too. Bun is a runtime as well as a package manager.

p: Name a Linux distribution.
source: Stack Overflow Developer Survey 2025 (Operating system)
metric: % of respondents naming it as an OS they use for personal use (SO 2025 operating-system question)
note: Personal-use column chosen; SO also reports professional use (e.g. Red Hat 5.7 professional vs 1.8 personal). ChromeOS and Android are included because the bank accepts them as answers.

p: Name a version control system.
source: Stack Overflow Developer Survey 2022 (Version control systems)
metric: % of all respondents who use it (2022 is the last SO survey that asked about VCS)

p: Name a backend web framework.
source: Stack Overflow Developer Survey 2025 (Web frameworks and technologies)
metric: % of all respondents who did extensive development work in it over the past year

p: Name a frontend JavaScript framework or UI library.
source: Stack Overflow Developer Survey 2025 (Web frameworks and technologies)
metric: % of all respondents who did extensive development work in it over the past year
note: SO lists AngularJS (7.2) separately from Angular; only "Angular" is used.

p: Name a web browser.
source: StatCounter Global Stats, browser market share worldwide, Sept 2026 (all platforms)
metric: % of worldwide page views (market share), September 2026
note: This is market share of page views, not % of people. Internet Explorer and others fall below StatCounter's reporting threshold.

p: Name a message broker or message queue system.
source: Stack Overflow Developer Survey 2024 (Other frameworks and libraries)
metric: % of all respondents who did extensive development work in it over the past year

p: Name a web server, application server or reverse proxy.
source: W3Techs web server usage
metric: % of websites (whose web server is known) using it, W3Techs 28 Oct 2026
note: Measures public websites, not developer usage. Cloudflare Server (32.9%) and Node.js (7.4%) lead but are not bank answers. Tomcat, Gunicorn, Uvicorn etc. are only listed as <0.1% (no number).

p: Name a JavaScript bundler, transpiler or build tool.
source: State of JavaScript 2024 (Build tools)
metric: State of JS 'usage' ratio x100: % of respondents to the item who have used it
note: Babel, Gulp and Grunt are not in the 2024 build-tools list. Data read from the page's page-data.json.

p: Name an API style or protocol for client-server communication.
source: Postman 2025 State of the API Report
metric: % of respondents using each API architecture

p: Name an in-memory cache or key-value store used by web backends.
source: DB-Engines Ranking of Key-value Stores, October 2026
metric: DB-Engines popularity score (not a percentage; Redis = 156.09)
note: A score, not a share: it combines web mentions, search interest, jobs etc. on a different scale from the survey entries. Managed services (ElastiCache, Memorystore) are not ranked.
